consensus_summary: No single settled primary meaning exists; 'tree' is polyvalent. Recognized senses cluster around a person/people (esp. the righteous) whose condition appears in fruit, the Tree of Life/eternal life, the cross, kingdoms/empires/rulers, Israel (fig/olive), the kingdom of God, and related ideas of judgment or wisdom; context selects the sense.
consensus_core_identification: polyvalent image (person/fruitfulness/Tree of Life/cross primary in most accounts; kingdoms/nations/people as common alternative)
boundary_disagreement: Book elevates nation/people as the identification, thereby excluding or demoting consensus cases such as the individual righteous person, Tree of Life, cross, mustard-seed kingdom, and fruitless judgment trees that the consensus admits as common or primary.
material_contradiction: None; consensus explicitly lists kingdoms, empires, rulers, nations, and covenant people (olive/fig) as attested senses, including the same Daniel 4 and Romans 11 passages.
rationale: All four consensus responses treat great trees or specific trees (olive, fig) as symbols of kingdoms, rulers, nations, or people as a common alternative, citing the identical Daniel and Romans texts. The book preserves that recognized referent while materially narrowing the polyvalent consensus field to this single category alone, producing a refined rather than contradictory or novel identification.
strongest_objection: Consensus uniformly insists on polyvalence and often ranks person/fruit, Tree of Life, or cross higher than nation/people; presenting the latter as the unqualified entry over-simplifies beyond mainstream recognition.
